learn.title: What these words mean
learn.confidence: Confidence is calculated from the measured evidence. It is not a severity.
learn.severity: Severity comes from the fixed policy for this detector. It is not the confidence.

pcap.name: PCAP
pcap.text: A file of captured packets. PCAPNG is the newer capture format. CyberTrace reads both and does not keep the raw file.

packet.name: Packet
packet.text: One frame on the network. CyberTrace keeps endpoints, sizes, timestamps, and selected metadata.

flow.name: Flow
flow.text: Packets that share a source, destination, ports, and transport protocol in one direction.

host.name: Host
host.text: An IP address observed in the capture, with its MAC addresses, counts, and timestamps.

ioc.name: IOC
ioc.text: An indicator copied from an alert, such as an IP, domain, URL, port, MAC, User-Agent, or timestamp.

alert.name: Alert
alert.text: A grouped finding with evidence, confidence, severity, and a status you can update.

finding.name: Finding
finding.text: One detector result. It exists only when the rule matched observed traffic.

confidence.name: Confidence
confidence.text: How strongly the measurement passed the detector threshold. A separate policy sets severity.

severity.name: Severity
severity.text: The fixed impact label for that detector: info, low, medium, high, or critical. Detectors do not choose it at random.

rule.name: Detection rule
rule.text: The named check, its threshold, and the evidence sentence that cites the observed values.

tcp.name: TCP
tcp.text: A connection-oriented transport. SYN and ACK flags are counted on each flow.

udp.name: UDP
udp.text: A connectionless transport. DNS often uses UDP port 53.

dns.name: DNS
dns.text: A name lookup. CyberTrace records the queried name when the packet contains one.

http.name: HTTP
http.text: Cleartext request metadata: method, host, path, and User-Agent. The body is not stored.

tls.name: TLS
tls.text: When a ClientHello is parsed, the server name is kept only if the SNI extension is present.

arp.name: ARP
arp.text: Address resolution on a local segment. A conflicting IP-to-MAC mapping is reported as suspicious, not as proof of an attack.

beaconing.name: Beaconing
beaconing.text: Repeated connections to one destination on a steady interval.

portScan.name: Port scan
portScan.text: A horizontal scan touches one port on many hosts. A vertical scan touches many ports on one host.

syn.name: SYN anomaly
syn.text: Many SYN packets toward one service without completed handshakes.

dnsAnomaly.name: DNS anomaly
dnsAnomaly.text: A long label, a high-entropy label, or a large number of distinct names from one source.

icmp.name: ICMP anomaly
icmp.text: Echo requests to many destinations, or an unusually large ICMP payload.

generic.what: A detector reported a measurement from this capture.
generic.why: The evidence lists the observed values. Compare them with the host owner before treating the event as an incident.
generic.verify: Open the same capture in Wireshark and filter on the IP, port, and protocol shown in the evidence.

horizontal_port_scan.what: One source sent SYN packets to the same port on many hosts.
horizontal_port_scan.why: That pattern can be a sweep for one service. It can also be an approved inventory scan.
horizontal_port_scan.verify: In Wireshark, filter tcp.flags.syn==1 && tcp.flags.ack==0 and the source IP, then look at the destination list for that port.

vertical_port_scan.what: One source sent SYN packets to many ports on one host.
vertical_port_scan.why: The source is probing which services answer. Confirm whether that test was authorized.
vertical_port_scan.verify: Filter the source and destination IP with tcp.flags.syn==1 && tcp.flags.ack==0 and count the destination ports.

network_scan.what: One source sent SYN-only probes to many hosts on more than one port.
network_scan.why: This is broader than a single-port sweep. A one-port sweep stays a horizontal port scan.
network_scan.verify: Filter the source IP and SYN packets without ACK, then compare the destination IP and port columns.

syn_burst.what: Many SYN packets went to one host and port without completed handshakes.
syn_burst.why: Unanswered SYNs can be a probe or a connectivity failure.

beaconing.what: Connections to one destination repeated on a steady interval.
beaconing.why: A steady interval can be a scheduled client. It can also be automated polling.
beaconing.verify: Follow the TCP or UDP stream and compare the time column between connections.

dns_anomaly.what: A DNS name was unusually long or high-entropy, or one source asked for many distinct names.
dns_anomaly.why: The evidence cites the length, entropy, or name count that crossed the threshold.
dns_anomaly.verify: Use the dns display filter and inspect the query name shown in the evidence.

icmp_anomaly.what: ICMP echo requests reached many destinations, or one payload was large.
icmp_anomaly.why: The evidence states the destination count or the payload size.
icmp_anomaly.verify: Filter icmp.type==8 and compare the destination list or the frame length.

cleartext_telnet.what: TCP port 23 was observed. The payload was not read.
cleartext_telnet.why: Telnet is a cleartext remote-login port. The finding is the port, not captured credentials.
cleartext_telnet.verify: Filter tcp.port==23. Do not expect CyberTrace to have stored the session contents.

cleartext_ftp.what: TCP port 21 was observed. The payload was not read.
cleartext_ftp.why: FTP control traffic is cleartext. The finding is the port.

large_outbound.what: An internal address sent a large byte count to a public address.
large_outbound.why: The evidence cites the observed byte count. Large transfers can be normal backups or unexpected exfiltration.
large_outbound.verify: Use Statistics > Conversations and compare the bytes for the pair in the evidence.

arp_multi_mac.what: One IP was announced by more than one MAC address.
arp_multi_mac.why: This is a suspicious mapping. It can be a NIC change, a misconfiguration, or spoofing. It is not proof of an attack.
arp_multi_mac.verify: Filter arp and compare the sender IP and sender MAC for the address in the evidence.

http_anomaly.what: An HTTP request crossed a measured threshold: URI length, method, URI count, a traversal marker, or User-Agent length or variety.
http_anomaly.why: A normal path such as /admin is not a finding by itself. The evidence names the measurement.
http_anomaly.verify: Filter http and inspect the request line and User-Agent. The body is not stored here.

custom_rule.what: A custom comparison matched an observed flow field.
custom_rule.why: The evidence shows the rule, the threshold, and the value taken from the flow.
custom_rule.verify: Find the same IP, port, and protocol in Wireshark and compare the count or bytes with the evidence.
